newsitem.title: UK: Coffee traders unfazed by LIFFE-LCE merger.
newsitem.headline: Coffee traders unfazed by LIFFE-LCE merger.

text.p: Coffee traders said Monday's merger between the International Finanical Futures Exchange (LIFFE) and London Commodity Exchange (LCE) would be mostly cosmetic for now with significant changes likely to be felt only after two years.
"The changes are all cosmetic as we are not yet under the same roof as LIFFE," said one former LCE now LIFFE coffee floor trader. That is expected about mid 1998.

The 40-year old LCE and the fast-paced LIFFE exchanges were officially merged on Monday, creating the only organisation in the world to trade a complete range of financial, commodity and equity futures and options.
The merger of the two exchanges was secured after LIFFE offered 10.3 million pounds for the LCE.
But coffee traders were unmoved, pointing to thin turnover of less than 1,000 lots in robusta coffee futures at midday.
"We listened to a few speeches about rules and behaviour...We were told swearing and abusive language are out," said the LIFFE coffee trader.
Traders said the LCE did have its own code of conduct, and fined traders 50 stg when caught swearing, but heftier fines were expected under the new LIFFE banner.
"The LIFFE guys swear all the time...But they earn mega bucks," said another dealer.
A LIFFE options trader was recently fined 500 stg for abusing a member of staff.
Aside from a new name and brightly-coloured jackets, coffee traders said little of substance had changed for them so far.
Higher turnover in commodities is expected when both exchanges operate under the same roof.
"The long-term benefit for the LCE and its existing members will come from the spillover business when we are co-located with LIFFE," Doug Humphris, director at Orebi Futures Ltd, said.
Humphris said Orebi, a non-clearing floor member of LIFFE, also intends to adopt a logo similar to that of the company's favourite football club, having received its permission.
"Our jackets will be superb," said Humphris.
After initial resistance to the idea, most floor coffee traders on Monday were doning the brightly coloured jackets which will remain the trademark of the crowded open outcry pits of LIFFE.
